title: Federated target translator autoscaler with per-tenant burst lockers and safety limits
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers with Dedicated fleets see noisy, bursty traffic patterns (chat sessions, embeddings storms) and require throughput guarantees. Current autoscalers use single-metric targets (p90 latency or token throughput) and reactive controllers that either overprovision or oscillate during short bursts. Goal: Implement a federated target translator that converts high-level throughput/latency SLOs into per-fleet and per-tenant scaling intents, while enforcing safety limits (max slew, committed headroom, eviction lockers) and supporting per-tenant burst credits that are spendable and renewable. The translator sits between the intent layer (SLAs/route configs) and the scaler core to produce stable, predictable capacity changes with fast but safe short-burst accommodation.
acceptance_criteria: Translator generates per-fleet scaling targets that meet configured throughput SLOs in >= 95% of synthetic load tests
Per-tenant burst credit system allows short bursts up to configured token budget without triggering fleet-wide overscale
Safety limits are enforced: max-slew rate prevents capacity increases > 30% per 5m window and max-decrease per 10m window; any violation is logged and triggers an alert
Canary rollout to 5% of fleets with observability dashboards showing target vs actual capacity, spend of burst credits, and violation events
Automated rollback criteria defined and tested (e.g., rising p95 latency > 2x baseline for > 3 minutes triggers automatic disable of translator)
Engineering docs, operator runbook, and unit/integration tests checked into repo with at least 85% coverage for core translator logic
design_decisions: Metric composition: use a weighted composite metric combining 95th latency, tokens/sec, and queue depth. We selected weights after offline tuning on 6 customer traces.
Scaling algorithm: model-predictive controller (MPC) for short-term forecasts (30s-5m) with a conservative PID fallback for noisy inputs.

Burst model: per-tenant burst lockers implemented as token buckets with configurable refill rates and maximum budget; lockers are federated to fleet-level reconciler to limit cross-tenant interference.
Safety fences: enforce three orthogonal limits - absolute max capacity per fleet, slew-rate caps (percent change per time window), and headroom floor tied to committed capacity contracts.
Fallbacks: if model confidence low or telemetry gaps detected, system will fall back to 'stability-first' mode which disables burst spend and applies a conservative step-up policy.
Observability: emit target_delta, predicted_demand, burst_spend, and safety_block_reason as top-level metrics and traces for each scaling decision
implementation_plan: 1) Build translator microservice scaffold behind feature flag (repo: github.com/redwood/rt-translator, branch: feat/federated-translator)
2) Implement composite metric engine + configurable weight schema and offline replay harness (unit tests + replay tests)
3) Integrate MPC library and expose tunable horizon/penalty params via config; implement deterministic fallback PID controller
4) Implement per-tenant token bucket lockers; persist short-term state in Redis with TTL and snapshot to primary datastore for auditing
5) Add safety limiter middleware that enforces fleet-level constraints and emits audit events to event-stream (kafka topic: fleet-safety-events)
6) Wire translator output into autoscaler operator (autoscaler accepts proposed_target_capacity + metadata), with dry-run mode to validate decisions without actuating capacity
7) Create dashboards (Grafana) and SLO checks (Prometheus rules) for canary monitoring
8) Open PRs for gradual rollout; coordinate with SRE for policy and alerting thresholds
tests_and_simulation: Replay tests using 6 anonymized customer traces (chat, embeddings, bursty API) to validate target stability and burst spend behavior
Load test in staging with mixed-tenant synthetic workload: steady baseline + random bursts (Pareto inter-arrival) to validate no fleet overshoot > 15% of expected capacity
Chaos tests: simulate telemetry gaps, Redis latency, and MPC internal failure to validate fallback paths
Safety fuzzing: randomized config inputs to ensure safety limiter never allows capacity beyond absolute contract limits
Metrics validation: ensure emitted predicted_demand correlates with actual tokens/sec within 20% under normal operation
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): enable dry-run translator for 10 fleets, collect dry-run telemetry for 3 days and review metrics
Phase 2 (Limited Actuation): enable actuation for 5% of fleets with per-fleet max-slew reduced to 15% for first 48 hours
Phase 3 (Gradual Expansion): incrementally increase fleet count to 30% over 2 weeks if canary metrics stable
Abort criteria: persistent p95 latency regression > 20% for > 5 minutes, burst_spend leading to > 10% extra cost vs baseline, or safety violations emitted > 1 per hour
Operator runbook: steps to disable translator, purge burst lockers, and revert autoscaler policy; include contact list for SRE and PM
notes: Budget: estimate additional monthly egress cost during canary ~ $2-3k due to safety headroom; finance notified
Follow-up work: integrate KMS-signed audit logs for burst locker spend history in next quarter
